claims.text: Replacing conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing with binder jet printing followed by low-temperature sintering will reduce residual thermal stresses in AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
Binder jet printing followed by low-temperature sintering will preserve a refined microstructure in AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
The proposed process will improve the mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
The temporary binder can be followed by low-temperature sintering in an inert atmosphere to consolidate the printed AlCrFeNiSi part.
Binder jetting and controlled low-temperature sintering impose lower energy input than conventional laser- or electron-beam-based additive manufacturing.
The proposed processing route reduces thermal gradients during fabrication.
Reduced thermal gradients minimize localized overheating.
Minimizing localized overheating lowers residual-stress accumulation.
Reduced thermal gradients and localized overheating produce a more uniform, refined microstructure.
Binder jet printing eliminates the rapid, high-temperature melting experienced in laser- or electron-beam-based additive manufacturing.
Low-temperature sintering can consolidate AlCrFeNiSi without inducing significant thermal stress.
Low-temperature sintering can consolidate AlCrFeNiSi without excessive grain growth.
Avoiding significant thermal stress and excessive grain growth alleviates degradation of mechanical properties.
Relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing, the proposed process will increase yield strength.
Relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing, the proposed process will increase ductility.
The hypothesis applies to miniature components processed by binder jet printing and low-temperature sintering under an inert atmosphere.
